title: Probabilistic golden-set gating + gradual traffic control and rollback orchestrator
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Problem: Current canary/A-B workflows use simple threshold alerts on aggregate eval scores which produce noisy flips and too-frequent full rollbacks. We need a more nuanced, statistically grounded gating engine that can: 1) combine multiple golden-prompt metrics into a single probabilistic alarm, 2) produce calibrated confidence intervals, 3) recommend traffic-control actions (throttle, partial rollback, block flip) rather than always doing a complete rollback, and 4) fit into the rollout orchestration path used by both hosted and Dedicated deployments.

Goal: Implement a 'Probabilistic Gating Engine' (PGE) that consumes golden-set scorecards and live shadow/canary outputs and emits graded signals with confidence. The PGE should support per-customer baseline calibration, multiple hypothesis correction across prompt-sets, and configurable action policies (auto-throttle, schedule human review, immediate rollback). Integrate PGE into the existing rollout-orchestrator API so canaries/A-Bs call a single endpoint to evaluate pass/fail and receive recommended actions and rationale.

Why unique: Unlike past tickets that build static scorecard alarms, this work couples statistical inference (bootstrap/CIs, Bayesian posterior deltas) with graded traffic controls and an explicit 'regret budget' mechanism that limits how much traffic an experiment may lose before manual intervention is required.
acceptance_criteria: PGE accepts a JSON scorecard payload and returns a pass/fail/graded recommendation with a confidence interval and top contributing prompts.
PGE supports at least two statistical backends: bootstrap CI and Bayesian posterior-delta, selectable per-project.
Rollout orchestrator uses PGE output to implement: 1) automated throttle (reduce new-canary-traffic by X%), 2) staged rollback (100% -> 50% -> 0) and 3) human-approval queue when configured.
Integration tests replay historical canary traces (one regression and one benign variance) and PGE recommendations match expected actions >95% of the time under configured thresholds.
New Grafana dashboard shows real-time PGE decisions, per-prompt contributions, and a 30-day calibration drift chart.
Ops runbook describing how to override/force flips and how to interpret PGE output is in Confluence.
design_decisions: Use stratified golden-sets: separate prompt buckets by token-length and intent label to avoid averaging-away regressions.
Default statistical backend: bootstrap percentile CI with 1,000 resamples for speed; optional Bayesian delta for low-volume customers.
Multi-metric aggregation via weighted linear combination where weights are configurable per-project; default weights tuned to precision-sensitive products (higher weight on hallucination-rate).

Action model: three tiers - WARN (log + annotate rollout), THROTTLE (cut new canary traffic by configured pct), ROLLBACK (initiate staged rollback). The orchestration engine accepts the recommended action and enforces it unless an allowlist/override is present.

False-positive control: require both a statistical signal (p<0.01 or posterior mass >95%) AND an effect-size minimum (delta > configured delta) to auto-rollback. Otherwise only throttle and require human approval.

Per-customer baseline: maintain an anchored baseline scorecard that decays with half-life configurable per project (default 30d); use this baseline to compute deltas and avoid drift mis-classification.

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy PGE in 'observe' mode for incoming canaries for 2 weeks; it will annotate but not alter traffic. Phase 2 (automated throttle): enable THROTTLE recommendations for internal customers with a conservative throttle cap (max 30%). Phase 3 (auto-rollback): enable auto-rollback for non-production namespaces where thresholds are aggressive; require human approval for P0 customers until 2 successful rollback drills are executed.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for statistical backends and aggregation rules. 2) Integration test that wires PGE to a stubbed rollout-orchestrator and verifies enforcement actions. 3) Replay test: feed recorded canary traces (one known regression, one noisy null) through PGE; assert recommended actions match expected. 4) Load test: verify PGE can evaluate a scorecard (1000 prompts) in < 1800ms under 95th percentile load.
risks_mitigations: Risk: over-sensitive auto-rollback causing customer-facing incidents. Mitigation: two-step requirement (statistical + effect-size) and per-customer allowlist that disables auto-rollback.
Risk: calibration drift causing false negatives. Mitigation: calibration drift chart, automatic baseline refresh with human sign-off, and decay half-life per project.
Risk: performance overhead on rollout latency. Mitigation: async evaluation for large golden-sets and cached recent evaluations for repeated identical payloads.
Risk: correlated prompts triggering multiple hypothesis errors. Mitigation: use BH correction by default when evaluating many prompt buckets and surface per-prompt contributions for manual review.
qa_steps: Deploy PGE to staging and run screenplay: apply a benign model change; assert PGE returns PASS and no enforcement action.
Insert synthetic regression into golden-set (increase hallucination rate); assert PGE returns THROTTLE or ROLLBACK per thresholds and top contributors are the synthetic prompts.
Simulate low-volume customer and validate Bayesian backend path produces stable posteriors and human-readable rationale.
Simulate high-volume canary and measure latency; ensure median < 800ms and 95th < 1800ms.
